goal: Determine the project-complexity frontier where direct, flat-state, minimal-CGNK, and full-CGNK execution differ in success, repair, context, token, and cost behavior.
acceptance_criteria: 24 formal generated-original project families cover eight project types and three complexity tiers
all four baselines use one frozen cheap Provider route and fixed budgets
formal attempts are captured in the local Project Corpus with private evaluator separation
aggregate results identify benefits, neutral effects, failures, and unsupported claims without changing default architecture
full repository regression has zero failures and zero errors

quality_metrics.target: 24 families, eight types, three complexity tiers, four matched baselines
quality_metrics.method: frozen formal manifest and aggregate matrix

quality_metrics.target: one model, fixed budgets, identical family contracts
all attempts captured; zero corrupt or unreferenced objects

quality_metrics.method: required gates, profiles, and full pytest

prevention: freeze source, route, schemas, contracts, and budgets
keep private evaluator packets outside Git
assurance: verify and rebuild the Project Corpus
run full repository regression and security/provenance audits
control: keep Router and Multi-Agent gates closed
improvement: test optional orchestration on deterministic complexity signals
add a dedicated cross-family capability reuse study

interface_expectations: Agent, CapabilityTree, ExecutionDAG, Project State, and public-delivery authorities remain unchanged
all formal baselines use the same qualified Provider model and public/hidden contracts
Project Corpus remains local application/evaluation infrastructure and never becomes a planning or execution authority
aggregate evidence may inform a future optional-orchestration study but cannot silently change the default runtime

feedback: one HIGH-complexity family failed identically under all four baselines
direct execution was the aggregate cost/token Pareto route
full orchestration benefit was neutral at the tested scale
the result supports optional-orchestration research but not a default architecture change

worked: frozen source, route, contracts, and budgets made the ablation comparable
local Project Corpus capture preserved all formal attempts and evidence lineage
public/private evaluator separation and sanitized aggregate publication prevented hidden-source leakage
did_not_work: the single HIGH library family remained wrong under all baselines
the current family set did not exercise enough cross-family capability reuse to support a reuse claim
experiments: LOW, MEDIUM, and HIGH complexity frontier
